title: Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid IX (ACSF.IX)
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.beppjdmn
materials: Calcium Chloride, dihydrate (CaCl2·2 H2O) (Sigma C3881, Sigma C3306 or equivalent)
D-Glucose (C6H12O6; aka Dextrose) (Sigma G7021 or equivalent)
Magnesium Sulfate, Heptahydrate (MgSO4·7 H2O) (Sigma M1880 or equivalent)
Sodium Phosphate monobasic monohydrate (NaH2PO4 • H2O) (Sigma S9638 or equivalent)
Potassium Chloride (KCl) (Sigma P9333, Sigma P5405 or equivalent)
Magnetic stir bar remover or additional stir bar
Warning: Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.
Table 1: Reagents required for preparation of 1L or 2L of ACSF.IX
Add reagents in order (top to bottom) as described in Table 1.
Allow all reagents to fully dissolve into solution before proceeding.
Dispose of excess reagents directly into municipal sewer system.

Rinse all beakers, graduated cylinders, and other equipment used to prepare ACSF solutions with MilliQ Water only (No Detergent). Invert all beakers and graduated cylinders and leave on clean absorbent pad to air dry.
Materials required for preparation of 2 Liters of ACSF.IX

steps.title: Label container and gather supplies
steps.instruction: Label a clean 1 L or 2 L polystyrene bottle (VWR 28199‑762) with the reagent name, preparation date, and preparer’s initials. Gather a stir bar, rinse it thoroughly with MilliQ water, and place it in the labeled bottle. Prepare a 0.45 µm filter system (VWR 28199‑976) and have a 1 L filter (VWR 28199‑814) ready. Note catalog numbers: NaCl (JT Baker 4058 or equivalent), Sodium Phosphate monobasic monohydrate, Magnesium Sulfate, Calcium Chloride dihydrate.

steps.title: Measure and add initial water
steps.instruction: Using a graduated cylinder, measure 1500 mL of MilliQ water and pour it into the labeled beaker containing the stir bar.

steps.title: Begin stirring
steps.instruction: Place the beaker on a stir plate and stir at a medium setting (≥400 RPM).

steps.title: Add calcium and magnesium salts
steps.instruction:
Choose the calcium/magnesium condition required for the experiment:
• If using 1.3 mM CaCl₂, add 1 mM MgSO₄.
   – MgSO₄: 246 mg for 1 L or 492 mg for 2 L.
   – CaCl₂·2H₂O: 191 mg for 1 L or 382 mg for 2 L.
• If using 2.0 mM CaCl₂, add 2.0 mM MgSO₄.
   – MgSO₄: 493 mg for 1 L or 986 mg for 2 L.
   – CaCl₂·2H₂O: 294 mg for 1 L or 588 mg for 2 L.
Allow the magnesium sulfate to dissolve completely before adding calcium chloride to avoid precipitation of divalent ions.

steps.title: Add sodium phosphate buffer
steps.instruction: Add Sodium Phosphate monobasic monohydrate: 172 mg for 1 L or 344 mg for 2 L of final solution.

steps.title: Add remaining ACSF.IX constituents
steps.instruction: Add the following reagents to achieve the concentrations listed for ACSF.IX (final 1 L or 2 L volume). Use the amounts calculated from the target concentrations (see table).

substeps.instruction: Magnesium Chloride – 1.0 mM (if required by formulation)
Magnesium Sulfate – 10 mM (baseline) plus the 1 mM or 2 mM added above
Sodium Phosphate monobasic – 1.2 mM (for 2 L) or 1.25 mM (for 1 L)
Potassium Chloride – 2.5 mM (or 3 mM/5.4 mM depending on formulation)
Sodium Bicarbonate – 25 mM (or 30 mM/18 mM as listed)
Sodium Chloride – 97 mM (or 126 mM/92 mM as listed)
Sodium L‑Ascorbate – 5 mM (or 0.16 mM for 2 L)

steps.title: Adjust final volume and pH
steps.instruction: Bring the solution to the final desired volume (1 000 mL or 2 000 mL) with MilliQ water using a volumetric flask. Adjust the pH to 7.3 if necessary.

steps.title: Measure osmolarity
steps.instruction: Take a 10 µL sample of the prepared solution and measure its osmolarity with an osmometer. Record the value; acceptable range is 285–305 mOsm (285–305 mmol kg⁻¹).

steps.title: Validate and document preparation
steps.instruction: If the measured osmolarity is outside 285–305 mOsm, discard the solution and remake it. Record the preparation date, all lot numbers (e.g., NaCl JT Baker 4058, filter VWR 28199‑976, etc.), and the measured osmolarity in the reagent preparation notebook. Wash the stir bar with MilliQ water after use.

steps.title: Store solution
steps.instruction: Store the finished ACSF.IX at 4 °C. The solution has a shelf life of one week; use it within one week of preparation or according to the investigator’s discretion.
